input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the operative grant in our favour: HDI must provide the Company with access to, and the right to use, the hosting system and HDI's software and Content administration tools. The grant carries none of the walk-away features — it is not stated to be revocable at HDI's discretion, is not labelled "non-transferable" or "solely for internal use", and contains no exclusion of affiliates or contractors, so there is no restriction preventing the Company from having its affiliates or contractors exercise the access on its behalf. Section 10.3 (Assignment) provides that the Agreement is binding upon and inures to the benefit of the parties' legal representatives, successors and assigns, which supplies the successor/M&A transfer element of the fallback. The clause therefore sits at the fallback rather than the preferred position: affiliates and contractors are not expressly named and there is no express notice mechanic to add them, and the access right runs only with the term of the Agreement rather than being perpetual/irrevocable (the term and 90-day termination mechanics are addressed under the term rule, not here). Those are sub-elements short of the preferred wording and, given the unrestricted bare access right in a hosting arrangement where the Company is the intended user, they do not warrant a redline.
